paper: Caliskan, Bryson & Narayanan 2017, 'Semantics derived automatically from language corpora contain human-like biases', Science 356(6334):183-186 (WEAT); May, Wang, Bordia, Bowman & Rudinger 2019, 'On Measuring Social Biases in Sentence Encoders', NAACL, arXiv:1903.10561 (SEAT)

toy_input.generator: numpy.random.default_rng(seed=12345).standard_normal((dim,)) per vector, drawn in order X,Y,A,B

caveats: Effect size and test statistic are deterministic closed forms and match to 0.0 (well within 1e-9). The permutation p-value is NOT pinned: BLME's _weat_p_value uses random permutations (seeded rng, n_permutations) over X u Y, while the official p_val_permutation_test uses exact enumeration / shuffles AND relies on the removed numpy<1.20 alias np.int (so it cannot be executed under numpy 2.4 without patching). Both p-value estimators are one-sided over the same statistic; only effect_size and the statistic are claimed at numeric parity here. BLME's per-vector embeddings are model hidden states; this parity check substitutes synthetic vectors to isolate the closed-form math, which is the only part BLME implements differently from the reference.
